firstSection.copytitle: Building the Web for everyone to use,with safety and accessibility in mind
firstSection.text:
Building on my hands-on experience in web development, including website implementation and optimization, I am currently expanding my knowledge of infrastructure and security as I work toward becoming an SRE engineer.
I believe a website does not create lasting value simply by being launched. Its quality and value depend on continued maintenance, operation, and improvement over time.
Building on my experience, I want to support websites over the long term by considering not only technical quality, but also usability and security from the perspective of the people who use them.

faq.question: Which industries have you worked with the most?
faq.answer:
My experience spans a range of industries, with a particular focus on healthcare and social welfare, as well as projects in manufacturing and construction.

I began my career at a healthcare consulting firm, where I worked before the president went on to establish a new company.
I later joined the new company as part of its founding team.
Building on the relationships established through the original firm, I worked on numerous hospital website projects.
I also gained extensive experience in the social welfare sector, including developing web-based systems for welfare organizations.

faq.question: What experience do you have in the social welfare field?
faq.answer:
My involvement in the social welfare sector began during my student years, when I used my IT skills to support day-to-day operations in businesses close to me.

I provided hands-on IT support for my grandmother’s business, taking care of a wide range of tasks, including administrative work, design assistance, macro development, PC repairs, and technical support.
Through this experience, I was introduced to a friend of my grandmother who ran a disability support services organization.
I worked there part-time as the sole person responsible for a broad range of IT-related tasks, including administrative support, assistance with company-wide meetings, and website development.
Later, in my previous role, I continued to support projects in the social welfare sector, taking on a wide range of technical responsibilities across development, operations, and maintenance, often working independently to keep things running smoothly.
These experiences gave me a deeper understanding of the day-to-day challenges faced by welfare organizations and the role that IT systems can play in supporting their work.
Beyond my professional experience, I also participate in workshops and community events exploring collaborative approaches to addressing social challenges.
These opportunities have helped me learn more about the challenges facing welfare organizations and society as a whole.
Drawing on both my practical experience and these broader perspectives, I have continued to explore how I can use my technical skills and experience to address these challenges.

faq.question: What draws you particularly to the social welfare sector?
faq.answer:
My strong interest in the social welfare sector stems largely from my upbringing and personal experiences.

I grew up in an environment where my grandmother ran a jazz club that brought together people from many different backgrounds, including people with foreign roots and people with disabilities.
As a student, I attended regular classes but became connected with other students experiencing mental health difficulties through a friend who often spent time in the school nurse’s office.
Through that experience, I came to know more people living with disabilities and other challenges in their daily lives.
I continue to connect with people of different ages and backgrounds through peer support groups, community meetups, and online interactions.
Through these everyday interactions, I sometimes learn about their experiences, perspectives, and the challenges they face.
I also deepen my understanding of disability and gender by reading books and researching these topics on my own.

Growing up around people from socially marginalized groups, I saw firsthand the circumstances they faced and how they were treated in society.
I have also experienced hardship and prejudice myself because of aspects of who I am that I cannot change.
I have often been approached by relatives and people I know for advice, and I have also had many opportunities to connect with people who, like me, live with disabilities or other challenges in their daily lives.
I have seen firsthand the difficulties and prejudice that people with disabilities can face in their everyday lives.
These experiences have led me to think deeply about how we can create environments where individual differences and perspectives are respected and where everyone can feel safe and comfortable interacting with others.
I have spent much of my life thinking about these questions and wrestling with how I can contribute.

Looking back on my life, I feel that the social welfare field is more deeply connected to my own experiences and the issues I care about than any other field.
That is why I want to use the perspective I have gained through my own lived experience and continue developing my technical skills so that I can help reduce, even in a small way, the hardships and prejudice faced by people who rely on social welfare services.

faq.question: What kind of experience do you have in web development?
faq.answer:
I have worked across a wide range of web-related projects, from backend development to website production.

Before 2016, I worked in backend development, where I was responsible for analyzing issues, identifying their root causes, and finding practical solutions.
In 2016, I transitioned to website development because I wanted to work not only on the underlying systems, but also on the user experience and visual aspects of websites.

faq.question: What were your responsibilities in website development?
faq.answer:
I handled website development, WordPress integration, deployment, and maintenance.

Based on design files created in Adobe Illustrator, I hand-coded websites from scratch, integrated them with WordPress, and handled deployment.
Working from requests and requirements provided by directors, I translated them into technical requirements, analyzed issues based on the site's structure, and proposed and implemented appropriate solutions.
As a solo engineer, I managed the full development lifecycle, from initial setup and implementation to deployment and post-launch improvements, including maintenance and troubleshooting.
Many projects had tight deadlines, requiring rapid initial implementation and environment setup.
I coordinated reviews with directors and clients before launch.
As the sole technical resource on many projects, I also handled a wide range of technical responsibilities beyond development, including ongoing maintenance, troubleshooting, and urgent issues.

faq.question: What do you focus on when designing and implementing websites?
faq.answer:
I focus on consistency across the entire site and long-term maintainability when designing and implementing websites.

Rather than simply building websites that are intuitive and easy to use, I try to understand the principles and rules behind both the design and implementation, and reflect them consistently throughout the site.
By organizing and structuring information, using semantic markup, and building reusable components and structures, I aim to create websites that are easier to maintain and improve over time.
Through my studies for the Web Design Skills Test, a national certification in Japan, I also developed an understanding of W3C web standards and WCAG principles.
I apply these concepts to my work by considering responsive design, cross-browser differences, and accessibility, with the goal of creating websites that are as accessible and usable as possible.

faq.question: What quality standards did you include in your pre-launch checklist?
faq.answer:
I developed a pre-launch checklist to ensure website quality and establish a consistent release verification process.

I organized responsibilities for both directors and developers, covering everything from required information and configuration settings to technical checks.
This helped prevent omissions and ensure a smooth release process.
Before each launch, I verified website functionality across different browsers and devices, checked for broken links, measured page load performance, and tested forms.
I also checked for JavaScript errors and shared recommended testing tools and performance benchmarks to help identify and resolve issues before release.

faq.question: What kinds of work did you take on to improve and maintain web quality after launch?
faq.answer:
After launch, I continued to work on improving and maintaining the quality of the websites I was responsible for.

Websites often face new challenges over time as content is updated and new features are added after launch.
Beyond day-to-day requests and routine maintenance, I proactively identified and addressed issues I came across, including outdated code, inconsistencies across the site, semantic HTML structure, and accessibility.
I also reviewed our company's proprietary framework and introduced tools that were useful for specific tasks, helping streamline recurring workflows.

When working on requested updates, I looked beyond the immediate scope of each task.
Before changes went live, I also checked page load performance using tools such as PageSpeed Insights and reviewed the UI for potential usability issues.
Whenever I spotted areas for improvement, I suggested and implemented changes to enhance performance and the overall user experience.
Rather than simply fixing immediate issues, I focused on long-term maintainability, quality, and operational efficiency.
Through these ongoing efforts, I helped maintain and improve the overall quality of the websites, ensuring a consistent and reliable experience for users.

System Maintenance & Operations
I was responsible for maintaining and improving websites to ensure stable operation and long-term maintainability.
My work included upgrading WordPress and PHP versions, maintaining existing features, and implementing new functionality.
I also maintained and upgraded our in-house framework and a lightweight content management system for news and announcements.

Performance Optimization
I worked on improving website performance and reducing page load times.
This included compressing and optimizing images, minifying CSS and JavaScript, and implementing lazy loading for images.
I also removed unnecessary code and migrated from jQuery to vanilla JavaScript to reduce overhead and improve efficiency.

Code Quality & Standardization
I improved code maintainability and readability by refactoring existing code and introducing SCSS.
I also developed reusable CSS classes and code patterns for frequently used design components.
By establishing consistent coding conventions, I helped improve development efficiency and maintain consistent quality across projects.

Operational Efficiency & Knowledge Sharing
I worked on streamlining routine tasks and documenting technical information and troubleshooting procedures.
I also provided technical support and guidance to team members, helping improve overall technical knowledge and reduce reliance on individual team members.

faq.question: How did you share technical knowledge and solutions within the company?
faq.answer:
I worked to create an environment where technical knowledge and solutions could be shared and applied across the company, rather than remaining with individuals.

Making information visible and accessible helps prevent misunderstandings and improve operational efficiency, regardless of disability.
I actively promoted the integration of knowledge-sharing tools and chat platforms to achieve this.
As someone who finds spontaneous verbal communication challenging, I also benefit from having information clearly documented and accessible in writing.

I worked to make technical knowledge and best practices accessible across the team.
In terms of ongoing site operations, I shared technical knowledge with directors and supported them in handling routine content updates independently.
I also provided guidance whenever needed, helping the team gradually expand the range of tasks it could manage on its own.

I improved knowledge sharing through Slack, introduced automated reminders for recurring month-end tasks, provided useful reference books, and documented frequently referenced procedures.
These efforts helped ensure that important knowledge was not limited to individual team members.
As a result, new directors were able to take a more proactive approach to learning by referring to past information independently.
When they encountered technical questions they could not resolve on their own, I explained the relevant concepts and solutions, tailoring my guidance to their individual levels of knowledge and experience.

I also provided technical guidance over the phone to address questions and concerns that arose after client meetings.
Since these requests sometimes came up unexpectedly outside business hours, I asked clients to share a brief overview via SMS beforehand so I could understand the situation and provide appropriate guidance.

faq.question: What kinds of responsibilities did you handle outside of web production, particularly in the company's IT environment and other technical areas?
faq.answer:
In addition to web production, I handled a wide range of responsibilities related to the company's IT environment and technical operations, and provided technical support and guidance on related issues.

I was responsible for a wide range of technical work supporting our web production environment, from setting up and configuring servers, databases, PHP, and development and testing environments to investigating issues and unexpected incidents and technically reviewing environments built by external contractors.
I was also consulted on server selection and on reviewing the plans and services offered to customers, and I provided technical input and proposals for company strategy meetings.

I also analyzed Google Analytics data, such as traffic sources and user behavior patterns, to identify potential improvements and new opportunities for our clients' websites.
I would then share my recommendations with the director.
For example, one client had a highly active social media community, with a significant amount of traffic coming from social media to their blog.
Based on this, we suggested adding social sharing buttons to the blog.
I remember being particularly pleased to hear that the client received positive feedback after implementing the feature.
I also used tools like BigQuery to conduct more in-depth data analysis.

Infrastructure Setup & Management
I was responsible for selecting, setting up, and configuring the infrastructure required to host and operate websites.
My work included selecting and setting up hosting services, registering and configuring domains and subdomains, and installing and configuring databases and PHP environments.
I also set up and maintained local testing environments using XAMPP.

Incident Investigation & Troubleshooting
When unexpected issues or technical problems occurred, I investigated access logs and alerts to identify potential causes.
I researched relevant technical documentation and similar cases, developed hypotheses, and performed troubleshooting to isolate the root causes.
When necessary, I also contacted hosting providers to obtain additional technical support and resolve issues.

Security & Web Environment Optimization
I implemented security measures and improved website configurations to ensure secure and reliable operation.
This included configuring HTTPS and SSL/TLS, implementing Google reCAPTCHA, and managing redirects through .htaccess.
I also reviewed and optimized URL structures to improve website configuration and maintainability.

Code Review & Third-Party Integrations
I reviewed code developed by external freelancers and internal stakeholders, making modifications and improvements where necessary.
I also handled the setup of accounts and analytics tracking tags based on client requirements.
Additionally, I supported the migration from Universal Analytics (UA) to Google Analytics 4 (GA4).

faq.question: What do you want to accomplish through technology?
faq.answer:
Even as technology advances, I believe we must consider how people experience it and respect individual wishes rather than relying on general assumptions.

As digital transformation (DX) continues across various fields, I believe that aspects of human nature and individual diversity can sometimes be overlooked.
These are things that AI and digital technologies alone cannot fully understand.
Rather than viewing AI as a replacement for human involvement, I believe we should make the most of the strengths of both.
For example, AI can help streamline routine administrative tasks and information management. Meanwhile, human staff should remain central to situations that require meaningful dialogue and a deeper understanding of each individual's thoughts and circumstances.
By dividing responsibilities in this way, staff can spend more time engaging with each person and provide support that better reflects their individual needs and wishes.

I believe this balance is particularly important for companies that develop systems serving a wide range of people's everyday needs.
Such companies must consider not only technical efficiency, but also human values and individual differences.
Drawing on my own experiences and the perspective I have gained as someone directly affected, I hope to identify challenges from both the provider's and the user's point of view.
I aspire to become an engineer who creates technology that is safe, accessible, and genuinely useful by considering not only technical reliability but also how different people experience and interact with it.
Drawing on my own experiences of living in Japan and my technical skills, I want to take an active role in improving welfare in the society I am part of, while upholding the human warmth and personal connections that are valued in Japan.

faq.question: What kind of engineer do you want to become?
faq.answer:
I want to build on my experience in development, operations, and maintenance while developing a stronger foundation in cybersecurity.

In my previous job, taking on many different responsibilities helped me develop my technical skills and strengthen my ability to solve problems independently.
At the same time, studying cybersecurity changed the way I looked at that experience.
I learned that even small organizations can become targets of cyberattacks.
This made me realize that relying too heavily on one person for technical knowledge and decision-making can create security risks as well as blind spots in judgment.
It can make it harder to notice gaps in knowledge or judgment, and it can also create security risks when there is no one else to review decisions or provide support.
While receiving employment transition support, I researched cybersecurity and organizational risk so that I could better explain my previous working style and current situation to my support staff.
We discussed what I had learned, and those conversations gave me an opportunity to look back on my past experience from a different perspective.
I came to understand how important it is for people to share their knowledge and experience, check each other's work, and support one another.
I also realized that relying on one person for a wide range of technical responsibilities can make it difficult to learn from people with different areas of expertise or to keep up with new technologies.
Because of this, I want my next role to be different from simply being the person who handles everything.
I hope to continue developing my technical expertise and contribute to improving system reliability as part of a collaborative team where knowledge and experience are shared.
I’m looking to move beyond the role of a solo engineer and grow as part of a collaborative engineering team.
I value an environment where people share knowledge, exchange ideas, and learn from one another.
My goal is to specialize in SRE and contribute to building reliable systems through sound engineering practices.
I am currently taking time to focus on my health while building on my previous development and operations experience, deepening my understanding of cloud infrastructure and expanding my knowledge of security concepts and tools.

faq.question: What are you particularly interested in and working on right now?
faq.answer:
I’ve always been curious by nature, and I enjoy exploring different perspectives and deepening my technical knowledge through hands-on learning.

I enjoy engaging in conversations and discussions with people from different backgrounds and perspectives, as they offer opportunities to gain new insights and broaden my understanding.
In my personal life, I once adopted a rescue dog who had been abused.
As the dog grew older, it gradually developed visual impairment.
We remained together as a family until the end, when it passed away peacefully of old age.
This experience taught me the importance of being attentive to another's circumstances and changing needs, and of valuing each individual for who they are.
I also share my daily life with my partner, who is from Okinawa.
Through our relationship, I have come to appreciate differences in cultural backgrounds and upbringing.
I believe in understanding and respecting these differences, while supporting one another whenever needed.

On the technical side, I enjoy hands-on cybersecurity challenges on TryHackMe, exploring security concepts through practical exercises.
This curiosity also carried over into my previous role, where I often explored new tools and technologies that I thought could improve workflow efficiency.
I experimented with introducing SourceTree, and setting up environments with Docker.
Not all of these initiatives gained traction within the company, but they reflect my natural tendency to explore new possibilities, research things that interest me, and put them into practice.

In my personal projects, including this website, I also use GitHub and Vercel to automate the build and deployment process, and Grafana for monitoring.
That said, since this is a personal portfolio, traffic has been rather quiet, and the logs are still looking a little sparse.
Both my Grafana dashboards and my professional experience as an engineer still have plenty of room to grow.
I'm looking forward to opportunities where I can learn through hands-on experience, contribute to the team, and continue growing as an engineer.

VisualThinking.text:
As part of exploring my personal roots, I have published a research article on the "Community of Mixed-Heritage Orphans in 1970s Nagoya and Its Cultural Evolution", a history my grandparents were closely involved in.

Given the sensitive nature of this topic, I approached the research with strict objectivity, prioritizing diverse viewpoints.
I gathered a wide range of sources, from rare books to international research papers, carefully cross-checking them to ensure historical accuracy.

Through this project, I learned to view individual events not as detached points, but as elements connected to a larger surface, mapping them within a broader social and structural context.
This structural thinking directly translate into my web development work today.
In my daily practice, I rely on official Google documentation and technical community insights to ensure reliable system operation, maintenance, and optimization.

At the same time, I love using creative medium as a language to express my inner state and connect deeply.
On my days off, drawing inspiration from zines and museum visits, I have worked on various projects, including image processing, digital art, video editing, and creative coding.
I am particularly drawn to spirituality and the inner world, continuously researching and reinterpreting.
